text:
Casey Cizikas has played 997 NHL games, every one of them for the Islanders, and Newsday's Andrew Gross has been chronicling the march toward 1,000. At 35, he is still doing the job he has always done: about 12 minutes a night of checking-line hockey, with 22 hits and very little scoring. He has 3 points in 19 games, 1 goal on 1.57 expected goals (the quality of chances he has generated).

The offense is quieter than last season, when he scored 10 goals, and the chances aren't there to suggest a bounce is coming: he is generating 0.41 expected goals per 60 minutes, down from 0.79 a year ago. The defensive side is the reason he still plays. Evolving-Hockey had opponents creating 0.18 fewer expected goals per 60 with him on the ice last season, 96th percentile among forwards. With him out there this season, the Islanders are getting just under half the shots and chances at five on five, which for a checking center is the point. The milestone is the story to watch this week.
